The species that nests on the old radar tower is the red-tailed hawk (Buteo jamaicensis) and Granite Ridge stands at 112 m elevation [rr-033:000]. The nest is on the south side, out of the prevailing wind [rr-079:000].

The reserve’s lead ammunition policy bans lead shot in 2019 and requires non-lead ammunition for visitors, staff, and researchers [rr-023:000]. In October 2024 the reserve treated an adult female peregrine named Juniper with a blood lead level of 0.42 ppm, above the 0.2 ppm threshold [rr-023:000]. The case cost USD 6,200 and is documented in rr-037 [rr-023:000].

The management plan target is to protect at least 90 percent of occupied raptor territories, with a baseline of 38 of 46 monitored territories in 2025 [rr-002:000]. In 2025, 38 of 46 territories were occupied [rr-043:000].

The ferry crossing takes 35 minutes [rr-056:001]; lighthouse tours are offered by booking a staff guide at the visitor center. The island is reached by the reserve ferry from Sable Point [rr-056:001]. The visitor center is open May-October, 9:00-17:00, and trails close at 19:00 [rr-056:001]. Groups of 10 or more must book at least two weeks in advance [rr-056:001].

The reserve operates 20 camera traps on a roughly 2 km grid and logged 4,100 trap nights in 2025 [rr-030:000]. The network recorded 1,240 raptor detections that year [rr-030:000]. No information about the number of trap nights or detections for 2026 is provided [rr-030:000].

The acoustic monitoring array has 12 stations and recorded 8,200 hours of audio in 2025 [rr-031:000]. The classifier flagged 1,840 raptor calls from that data [rr-031:000]. No information about the number of hours is provided for 2026.
